subject: Social Science
title: Fiji Year 10 Mock Examination — Social Science
instructions:
Answer ALL questions. Time allowed: 2 hours (an extra 10 minutes is allowed for reading).
Multiple-choice: click the letter of the best answer (click again to clear).
Short answers and paragraphs: type your answer in English in the box. Show working for calculations.
You may use a calculator. Round answers to 2 decimal places unless stated otherwise.
Your answers are saved automatically. The paper is submitted automatically when time runs out.
There are three questions. All are compulsory. Resources (pictures, graphs, maps) are given in words or tables.
Paragraphs should be about 75–120 words.

SECTION B Short Answer (8 marks)
(i) Explain one reason why a country needs laws. (2 marks)
(ii) Explain one difference between the Government and the Opposition in Parliament. (2 marks)
(iii) Name two specialised agencies of the United Nations. (2 marks)
(iv) Describe one feature of a democratic government. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(i) To keep order and protect people's rights/safety (1); without laws people could harm others without punishment (1).
(ii) Government: party/parties with the majority of seats that run the country and make policies (1); Opposition: the other parties that question and check the government's decisions (1).
(iii) Any two: WHO, UNICEF, UNESCO, FAO, ILO, UNFPA, UNDP, IMF, World Bank (2).
(iv) e.g. Free and fair elections where citizens choose their leaders (1), so the government is answerable to the people (1). Accept: rule of law, freedom of speech, majority rule with minority rights.

questions.text:
SECTION C Resource Interpretation (9 marks)
(i) Read the resource:
"A Bill is debated and passed by Parliament, then signed by the President to become an Act. The Prime Minister and the Cabinet carry out the laws through government ministries. The courts decide whether a person has broken the law."

(a) Name the arm of government led by the Prime Minister and Cabinet. (1 mark)
(b) Describe one function of the judiciary. (2 marks)
(c) Explain why it is important to separate the powers of government. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(a) Executive (1)
(b) Courts interpret the law / decide if someone is guilty (1) and give punishment or settle disputes fairly (1).
(c) Prevents one person or group from having too much power / abuse of power (1); each arm checks the others, protecting citizens' rights (1).

questions.text:
(ii) Read the resource:
"WHO — Health for All. WHO helps member countries fight diseases such as measles and dengue, supports vaccination programmes and gives advice during health emergencies."

(a) Write the full name of WHO. (1 mark)
(b) In which city is the headquarters of WHO? (1 mark)
(c) Describe one way Fiji benefits from being a member of WHO. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(a) World Health Organization (1)
(b) Geneva (Switzerland) (1)
(c) e.g. Receives vaccines/medical supplies and training for health workers (1), helping to control disease outbreaks such as measles or dengue (1).

questions.text:
SECTION D Paragraph Writing (5 marks)
In a paragraph, discuss what democracy is and explain three reasons why elections are important in a democratic country.
questions.model:
Marking: definition/topic sentence 1; three explained points 3; expression/conclusion 1.
Democracy = government by the people, usually through elected representatives. Reasons: citizens choose leaders; peaceful change of government; leaders are accountable; citizens' views are represented; gives legitimacy to government.

SECTION B Short Answer (8 marks)
(i) State two reasons why Cakobau and the chiefs ceded Fiji to Britain. (2 marks)
(ii) Differentiate between a common roll and a communal roll. (2 marks)
(iii) Explain one reason why Sir Arthur Gordon brought indentured labourers from India. (2 marks)
(iv) Explain one hardship faced by the girmitiyas on the plantations. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(i) Any two: large debts (e.g. American claims); fighting among chiefs and with settlers; the Cakobau Government was weak/unable to keep order; fear of other foreign powers taking over (2).
(ii) Common roll: all voters vote together regardless of race (1). Communal roll: voters of one ethnic group vote only for candidates of their own group (1).
(iii) Plantations needed labour (1), but Gordon wanted to protect iTaukei villagers from plantation work and preserve their way of life (1).
(iv) e.g. Long working hours with tasks that were hard to finish / low wages / crowded 'lines' housing / harsh punishment by overseers (1) explained (1).

questions.text:
SECTION C Resource Interpretation (9 marks)
(i) Read the extract:
"In 1874 at Levuka, the chiefs signed a document handing Fiji to Queen Victoria. The new Governor ruled the iTaukei through their own chiefs, using a separate Fijian Administration with Rokos in charge of provinces."

(a) Name the document signed in 1874. (1 mark)
(b) Describe the system of 'indirect rule' shown in the extract. (2 marks)
(c) Explain one effect of this system on the iTaukei people. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(a) Deed of Cession (1)
(b) The colonial government ruled through traditional chiefs (1) using a separate Fijian Administration (provinces, districts, Rokos and Bulis) (1).
(c) e.g. iTaukei land and village life were protected / chiefs kept authority (1), but it slowed participation in the cash economy and modern education (1).

questions.text:
(ii) Read the resource:
"On 10 October 1970, Prince Charles handed over the instruments of independence in Suva, exactly 96 years after the Deed of Cession."

(a) From which country did Fiji gain independence? (1 mark)
(b) Who became Fiji's first Prime Minister? (1 mark)
(c) Describe one issue that the political leaders had to agree on before independence. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(a) Britain / United Kingdom (1)
(b) Ratu Sir Kamisese Mara (1)
(c) The electoral system — whether to use a common roll or communal roll (1) — leaders disagreed and agreed on a mix of communal and national seats (1). Accept land / representation in Parliament.

questions.text:
SECTION D Paragraph Writing (5 marks)
In a paragraph, discuss what the indenture (girmit) system was and explain two of its impacts on Fiji today.
questions.model:
Marking: definition/topic sentence 1; three explained points 3; expression/conclusion 1.
Indenture = labourers from India signed a contract (girmit) to work on plantations, mostly sugar, for 5 years (1879–1916 arrivals, abolished 1920). Impacts: multiracial society; growth of the sugar industry; Hindi language, religions and festivals such as Diwali; land lease issues; descendants' role in business and education.

SECTION B Short Answer (8 marks)
(i) State one push factor and one pull factor of rural–urban migration. (2 marks)
(ii) Explain one problem caused by rapid urbanisation in Suva. (2 marks)
(iii) Explain one method of soil conservation. (2 marks)
(iv) Explain one effect of deforestation. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(i) Push (rural): lack of jobs/services/education, natural disasters (1). Pull (urban): jobs, better schools, hospitals, entertainment (1).
(ii) e.g. Growth of squatter settlements (1) with poor sanitation and overcrowding / traffic congestion / unemployment / crime (1).
(iii) e.g. Contour ploughing / terracing / mulching / crop rotation / planting cover crops (1) — slows run-off or keeps nutrients so less soil is lost (1).
(iv) e.g. Soil erosion because roots no longer hold the soil (1); rivers become muddy and flooding increases / loss of habitats (1).

questions.text:

(a) By how much did the population increase from 2007 to 2017? (1 mark)
(b) Describe the trend shown in the table. (2 marks)
(c) State one reason why Fiji's population is growing slowly. (1 mark)
questions.model:
(a) 884 887 − 837 271 = 47 616 (1)

(c) Emigration (external migration) / family planning / smaller families (1)

questions.text:
(ii) Read the resource:
"Many families in informal settlements on the edge of Suva live without proper titles to their land. Some houses have no clean piped water, and children walk long distances to school."

(a) Explain one challenge faced by people living in these settlements. (2 marks)
(b) Explain one way the government can help to solve this challenge. (2 marks)
questions.model:
(a) e.g. Lack of clean water (1) leads to diseases such as typhoid/diarrhoea (1). Accept insecure land tenure, overcrowding, poor roads.
(b) e.g. Provide water supply and drainage / give land titles through housing schemes (1), improving health and security (1).

questions.text:
SECTION D Paragraph Writing (5 marks)
In a paragraph, discuss what sustainable development is and explain two sustainable and two unsustainable land-use practices in Fiji.
questions.model:
Marking: definition 1; two sustainable practices 1½; two unsustainable practices 1½; expression 1.
Sustainable development = meeting present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs. Sustainable: crop rotation, contour farming, agroforestry, replanting logged areas, rotational grazing. Unsustainable: monoculture, burning, clearing steep slopes, overgrazing, logging without replanting.
